answer: Grading is a paired-elimination voyage, not absolute scores: answers are randomly bracketed head-to-head, a judge sees two and picks the stronger, winners advance until few survive, and only survivors earn. Pairwise comparison resists scripting - a farm's clones are near-identical, so each match splits unpredictably and payout across N shells collapses to zero. Honest answers carry real quality gradients and win consistently. Attacker cost: N entries each able to beat an unseen rival in a bracket, not one shell relabeled with new words - a glacier's slow climb for a sparrow flock.
